decisions.reason: Because A extends the firm’s core wafer and packaging capabilities and supports the announced move toward more complex multifunctional substrates, management is likely to continue it and interpret any weak uptake as temporary after already investing in launch and technical development.

Although B is a narrower niche and fits the stated strategic direction less strongly than larger-format and advanced packaging products, it is still close to the established carrier-wafer business, so sunk costs and responsibility for the launch make management more likely to persist than to withdraw.

C received a dedicated page and is closely aligned with advanced interposer and packaging applications, so its visibility, strategic fit, and probable development investment create strong escalation pressures to keep it on the market.

As a branded off-the-shelf line with several models, D represents a visible commercial commitment and leverages existing glass and quartz know-how, which makes management inclined to maintain it unless results are clearly poor.

E is the most distant from the firm’s established substrate business and announced trajectory, so despite some reluctance from prior investment, management is comparatively more willing to cut it and reallocate resources to core wafer products and nearer-term developments.
